mint pulls only msg.sender underlying, credits only msg.sender pUSDC using actual balance increase and a floored exchange-rate division. redeem burns caller pUSDC and floors underlying output; redeemUnderlying calculates the pUSDC debit using floored division. There is no caller output minimum, input maximum or deadline; small-amount rounding and changing exchange rates matter.

borrow increases only msg.sender debt and sends underlying to that caller; comptroller collateral/liquidity checks and available cash apply. Collateral-market entry, approvals and token transfers are not granted here, so this is not a complete borrowing workflow.

repayBorrow pulls caller funds to reduce caller debt; repayBorrowBehalf pulls only caller funds to reduce the named borrower debt and confers no authority over that borrower. uint256 max is the current-full-debt sentinel. An amount greater than current debt can revert on subtraction; transfer-fee balance differences affect actual credited payment.

Each selected method accrues interest first. Interest model rate, elapsed blocks, configurable minInterestAccumulated and reserveFactor affect debt/reserves; suppliers receive the net exchange-rate result (cash + borrows - reserves) / pToken supply, not guaranteed principal or yield. This implementation has no separate ordinary user entry/exit fee in the selected bodies.

Compound-style uint return values are error codes (0 succeeds); a transaction can succeed at the EVM level yet return a financial failure and emit Failure. Source-dependent comptroller, oracle, listing, pause, cap, collateral and cash checks still determine execution. No queued or guaranteed exit is implied.
